svg.title: Fig. 100 — y = x^(1/x), with the dotted branches
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 100, page 105. Section: discontinuous.

g.data-text: The axes and the two dashed lines y = 1 and y = −1, the limits of x^(1/x) as x → +∞ and of the negative branch.
For x > 0 the curve leaves the origin (x^(1/x) → 0 as x → 0+), rises to its maximum e^(1/e) ≈ 1.44 at x = e and sinks slowly to the asymptote y = 1.

For x < 0 the power is defined only at rational x with odd denominator and has either sign: the points lie on the dotted curves ±|x|^(1/x), which tend to ±∞ as x → 0− and cross the dashed lines at x = −1; the lower dotted curve for x > 0 is −x^(1/x).
